validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solid. The Arab Gas Pipeline (AGP) Phase-1 Egyptian overland leg from El Arish (North Sinai, Mediterranean coast) across the Sinai peninsula to Taba (South Sinai, Gulf of Aqaba) is heavily documented; commissioned July 2003. Independently confirmed by offshore-technology.com (Verdict Media project page) and thenationalnews.com (2021 explainer), plus Wikipedia. Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correct - a high-pressure gas transmission trunk (36-in, cross-Sinai export trunk feeding the Taba->Aqaba subsea crossing and onward to Jordan/Syria/Lebanon), not gathering/process. DUPLICATE: NOT a duplicate. P0436 is the 250 km Arish->Taba OVERLAND segment; the separate P7482 (Arab Gas Pipeline, Taba->Aqaba, 18 km) is the ~15 km subsea Gulf-of-Aqaba crossing - a legitimate sibling segment, not a double-count (RouteNotes 'IM: updated 2025 to reflect individual segment' documents the deliberate split). P0462 (Arish->Ashkelon, EMG line to Israel) shares the Arish origin but is a physically different pipeline. GulfPub lumps 'Arab Gas Pipeline | El Arish -> Aqaba' into one 169 km/36-in operating record - that corroborates existence/diameter/status but its 169 km is wrong (real Arish-Aqaba total ~265 km = 250 overland + ~15 subsea) and its operator 'East Mediterranean Gas Company' is a GulfPub confusion with the EMG (Arish-Ashkelon) company. ATTRIBUTION: GEM's Operator=Egyptian Natural Gas Co (GASCO) / Owner=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS) 100% is correct - offshore-technology names the Egyptian developer consortium as EGAS, ENPPI, Petrojet and GASCO. GulfPub's EMGC is wrong; prefer GEM. SPEC: length 250 km (overland), diameter 36 in, capacity 10.3 bcm/y (=360 bcf/y), start 2003, proposal 2001 - ALL corroborated by offshore-technology and The National (two independent origins; note offshore-technology and the sheet's hydrocarbons-technology ref are the same publisher, so I used The National as the second independent origin). Only weak point: SegmentCost 207,550,000 USD - the cited hydrocarbons-technology page no longer surfaces that number (existing_ref_check failed) and independent sources give the phase-1 investment as ~USD 220 million, so the exact 207.55M figure is unsupported; flagged for human, not auto-changed.

routes.start_name: El Arish (Arish compressor/metering station, North Sinai, Mediterranean coast), Egypt
routes.end_name: Taba (Gulf of Aqaba landfall / metering station, South Sinai), Egypt
routes.corridor_desc: Overland trunk crossing the Sinai Peninsula on a roughly NW->SE diagonal, from El Arish on the North Sinai Mediterranean coast down to Taba at the northern tip of the Gulf of Aqaba, ~250 km. Endpoints are firmly sourced named facilities (Arish compressor station -> Taba, where it hands off to the ~15 km Taba->Aqaba subsea crossing, P7482). The precise interior alignment across central Sinai is NOT independently sourced, so treat the interior as an approximate great-circle-ish corridor between the two firm endpoints; no interior waypoint coordinates asserted (none fabricated).
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from offshore-technology ('250 km overland pipeline from Arish to Taba on the Red Sea') and The National; Arish and Taba coordinates are real, well-known city/facility locations (EPSG:4326). Interior Sinai path unsourced -> left without waypoints rather than invented; corridor bound is the endpoint pair plus the documented cross-Sinai orientation, hence suggested medium (endpoints firm, interior approximate).

summary: P0436 Arab Gas Pipeline (Arish-Taba overland, 250 km/36 in/10.3 bcm/y, 2003) CONFIRMED - existence/classification/specs corroborated by 2 independent sources; caveats: GulfPub misattributes operator (EMGC) and length (169 km) vs GEM's correct GASCO/EGAS + 250 km, and SegmentCost 207.55M USD is unsupported (~220M cited).
